In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of the sulfonamide moiety in the pyridinium derivative is crucial in determining the conformance and the binding affinity of the compound to the enzyme, while the presence of a substituent on the pyridinium nitrogen atom does not affect the conformation of inhibitor but the binding affinity.
the pyridinium moiety is the key feature in the design of sulfonamides with a selective inhibitory activity towards hCA II.
the pyridinium sulfonamides are a new class of CAIs that, thanks to their peculiar structural features, can be designed with an isoform-selective inhibition profile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a pyridinium sulfonamide CA inhibitor, with a bulky triphenylpyrydinium moiety, binds to hCA II in a different conformation with respect to other CA isoforms and to a similar pyridinium inhibitor with a smaller phenyl group.

a sulfonamide inhibitor with the pyridinium moiety is able to form an adduct with human CA II, in which the pyridinium nitrogen is involved in the formation of the adduct with the zinc ion of the enzyme.
we have determined the structure of the hCA II adduct with an isoform selective inhibitor, which is a membrane impermeable, pyridinium derivative.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the substitution of a pyridinium ring in the sulfonamide moiety of the inhibitor can be a key feature to modulate the binding affinity of the inhibitor towards the enzyme.
a pyridinium derivative can be used as a template for designing new CAIs, and that the substitution pattern of the pyridine ring plays a key-role in the binding affinity to CA isoforms.
pyridinium derivatives of sulfonamides are able to bind CA isoforms with a high selectivity profile.
